name: l2_merge
supersedes: protocol.json (v1) only for the field delivered_bytes_per_cycle; window_cycles and max_requests_per_read stay as installed from v1 (h100-r1 / b300-r2)
mechanism: memory.l2_merge.delivered_bytes_per_cycle (GPU-shared, full-GPU loop: docs/en/design/mechanism-tree.md). Engine definition (cpp/core/memory_hierarchy.cpp load(), cfg_.merge_bytes_per_cycle): when an L1-missing sector request is merged into an open same-sector merge entry it does not go to L2 / DRAM; it completes at max(leader completion, merge delivery queue), where the single GPU-wide delivery queue is charged sector_bytes / delivered_bytes_per_cycle per merged sector. The quantity is therefore the GPU-wide ceiling on the rate at which merged (slice-read-shared) sectors are delivered to SMs, in bytes per SM cycle.
installed: h100 12743.5 = hopper-prototype M1 r4 scan ld_l2g_24mb_g004_lock_stride2mb (25228.3 B/ns at 1979.8 MHz, source hopper.17a05956f82b13ac352f95d5, artifact rebuild/fg/s3r2/m1_r4/scan/results.json); b300 0 = no cap (v1 b300-r2 unrealised: the TMA probe aggregate is bound by the per-SM stream rate, addendum 2026-11-05 in protocol.json)
why_v2: the v1 TMA probe (one issuing thread, 4 x 16 KiB ring) is latency-bound per SM (30.8 / 28.3 B/cycle/SM) and its aggregate never approaches the delivery ceiling. The predecessor value came from a 1024-thread LDG.E.128 streamer where G CTAs read the same slice in lockstep and the SM-side aggregate (up to 97 B/cycle/SM) exceeds the disjoint-slice L2 read rate (29 B/cycle/SM): the excess is merged delivery.
probe: tools/microbench/l2_merge/probe/ldg_scan.cu = hopper-prototype tools/microbench/l2_dram_scan_microbench.cu (hopper-prototype main@e9ba55e5) verbatim except: the nsm upper bound 132 becomes the device's multiProcessorCount (queried at runtime, same change as the v1 tma_scan port). Mode ld, region=slice, 1024 threads per CTA, one CTA per SM, ld.global.cg.v4 (SASS LDG.E.128.STRONG.GPU) UNROLL 8; the footprint (24 MB, L2-resident on both devices) is split into nsm / G disjoint slices and the G consecutive CTAs of a slice stream the same addresses from the same start (lockstep; no barrier, launch order only); every CTA streams per_cta_mb = 256 MB; per-CTA clock64 / %globaltimer give bytes per SM cycle and the aggregate over the union window (RESULT agg_B_per_ns, per_sm_B_per_cycle median, mhz = median per-CTA cycles / ns). Runner: run_scan.py --set m1r4 (configs below; nsm(G) = floor(SM count / G) x G; h100 132 SMs: 132 for every G; b300 148 SMs: 148 / 148 / 144 / 144 / 132 / 132 / 132 / 132 at G 2 / 4 / 6 / 12 / 22 / 44 / 66 / 132). Every config runs --trials 5 (trial 0 warm-up excluded by the probe) and once under ncu (--cache-control none --clock-control none, kernel regex scan_kernel, launch-skip 1 launch-count 1, metrics as v1 plus l1tex__t_bytes.sum).
sass_gate: cuobjdump (h100: -xelf all on the binary, then -sass on every extracted cubin; b300: the same) must list the ld streamer kernel (scan_kernel<false>, the `ld` instantiation) and it must contain exactly UNROLL = 8 LDG.E.128 instructions in its stream loop and no other LDG.E.128 (the predecessor's sass_check line `stream: LDG.*128 x8`); 0 kernels listed or a different LDG.E.128 count fails the gate and the run is unrealised. Written to <run>/build/sass/ldg_scan.sass and sass_check.txt.

cells.lock_g: ld_l2g_24mb_g{G}_lock, G in {2, 4, 6, 12, 22, 44, 66, 132}, nsm(G) as above, threads 1024, footprint 24 MB, per_cta 256 MB, region=slice group=G (the predecessor's r4 (b) lockstep set)
cells.lock_g_stride2mb: ld_l2g_24mb_g{G}_lock_stride2mb, G in {2, 4, 12, 44}: same with slice_stride_mb=2 (every slice on a 2 MB boundary; the predecessor's r4 (c) set, which gave the installed maximum)
cells.rot_g: ld_l2g_24mb_g{G}_rot, G in {2, 4, 6, 12, 22, 44, 66, 132}: group_rot=1 (members start at rotated offsets so they are not on the same lines at once): reported as the unmerged control of the same slice layout
cells.disjoint: ld_l2s_24mb_t1024_n{SM count}_base: group 1, one slice per CTA (no sharing): per-SM L2 stream rate reference r = 1

derivation.validity: a config is valid only if rc 0, PLACEMENT distinct_sm == nsm (active_sms == nsm) and the ncu launch rc 0; invalid configs are excluded and listed
derivation.r: r(config) = lts__t_bytes.sum / l1tex__t_bytes.sum of the ncu launch (slice-side bytes per SM-side bytes; 1 = no merging, 1/G = every slice read serves all G requesters)
derivation.delivered_bytes_per_cycle: max over the valid lock_g and lock_g_stride2mb configs of agg_B_per_ns x 1000 / mhz (RESULT line; median over trials); the attaining config, its r and the whole table are reported. The attaining config must have r <= 0.75 (merging demonstrably present) and its aggregate must exceed the disjoint reference aggregate by >= 20 %, otherwise the cell is unrealised (the maximum would be the unmerged L2 stream rate, not merged delivery)
derivation.other: rot_g aggregates, per-SM B/cycle of every config, the disjoint reference rate, and dram__bytes_read.sum (must be << lts bytes: footprint L2-resident) are reported

acceptance.measured: the two runs' delivered_bytes_per_cycle within 5 % of each other (relative to their mean); the attaining configs need not be the same G; sass gate passed; references valid
acceptance.experimental: two runs within 5..15 %: installed as experimental with both run values in the source
acceptance.unrealised: two runs differ by > 15 %, or the attaining config fails the r <= 0.75 / +20 % conditions in either run, or the sass gate fails, or more than one lock config invalid: reported, leaf unchanged

runs: two runs per device (run-a, run-b) in one job, --trials 5; run dirs $A/microbench/l2_merge/h100-r3 and b300-r4 (h100-r2 / b300-r3 = failed build / gate, addendum) (SET=m1r4), model $A/microbench/l2_merge-model/<device>-<run>/model.json (model_v2.py)
install: memory.l2_merge.delivered_bytes_per_cycle on both devices (bytes per SM cycle): h100 replaces the hopper-prototype 12743.5 (source hopper.17a05956f82b13ac352f95d5 removed) when the cell passes; b300 replaces 0 (source l2_merge.b300.r2.delivered_unrealised removed); source keys l2_merge.<device>.<run>.delivered with protocol tools/microbench/l2_merge/protocol-v2.json. A/B: single-cluster 450 both architectures recorded with the note that this leaf belongs to the full-GPU loop (single-cluster jobs rarely merge across SMs; the full-GPU round is outside this line)
engine_note: the engine's delivery queue is a single GPU-wide FIFO charged per merged sector; the hardware quantity is the SM-side aggregate of merged + unmerged delivery under maximal sharing. The probe maximum includes the unmerged slice reads (1/G of the bytes); the protocol installs the aggregate as the predecessor did and reports the merged-only share (agg x (1 - r)) for the engine line
not_allowed: no case-cycle tuning; no values from other machines; no threshold or derivation change after data; no install without the ncu cross-check and the sass gate

addenda.name: read_domain
addenda.written: before any data of these cells; the candidate 'block' below was formed after looking at the cp.async shared_read_domain data (ldgsts_loaded protocol) and its recorded SM ids, so for cp.async it is a re-reading of seen data and only the new cells test it
addenda.text: Question: inside which set of SMs is an L2 read shared, for TMA tile loads (never measured with members that are not consecutive CTAs) and for cp.async. Why: with the installed pair domain (memory.l2_merge.domain_sms = 2) the simulated TMA kernels share nothing across pairs, and several became slower than hardware (full-gpu r22); hardware counters of kernels sit between the old GPU-wide rule and the pair rule (srcunit_tex reads per delivered sector: cublas_bf16_bigK_00 0.500, cutlass_sparse_00 0.715, B300 cuBLASLt 2-CTA kernels 0.71-0.73, CUF-C76-CONV-WGRAD-S02 0.70, where r22 simulates 0.94-1.00 and r21 0.24-0.56). Re-reading of existing data (after seeing it): a full grid is dispatched in blocks of 4-5 SM pairs (H100 ids 0..63: {b, b+16, b+32, b+48} pairs; 64..119: 4 pairs with id stride 14; B300 ids 0..79: 5 pairs; 80..135: 4 pairs stride 14; the highest ids separately), two blocks per sm_topology placement_domain on most ids. 'Any two SMs of one block share a read' reproduces the single-bit cp.async cells the pair rule left unexplained: bit 4 predicted 0.758 | 0.784 (h100 | b300) against measured 0.77-0.79 | 0.79-0.81, bit 5 0.727 | 0.784 against 0.74-0.77 | 0.79-0.82, bit 6 1.000 | 0.892 against 1.009 | 0.892, bit 1 0.970 on h100 against 0.976; and with at most N = 4 requests per read the grouped cells within 0.07 (h100 M31 / M63 / M255 0.273 / 0.258 / 0.258 against 0.32-0.35 / 0.33 / 0.31; b300 0.311 / 0.297 / 0.290 against 0.31-0.37 / 0.29-0.32 / 0.26-0.29). Against it: b300 bit 1 measured 1.000 where one block of ids 142..147 predicts 0.987. The existing cells cannot tell a block from a placement domain (no cell pairs the two blocks of one domain). Counter note from the kernel data: lts__t_sectors_op_read also counts reads arriving over the L2 fabric and exceeds the sectors delivered when the data is not L2-resident (r_all up to 1.5 on cold kernels), so kernels are read with lts__t_sectors_srcunit_tex_op_read; on these L2-resident probes both are reported and r_all stays the declared ratio. Probe changes: tma_scan gets table=<file> (slice and member by SM id), far=1 (group members nsm / group apart in block index) and log=<file>; ldgsts_loaded gets --table and writes the stream cycles and start of every CTA. Tables and predictions: domain_tables.py (candidates pair / block / gpc, predicted ratio = sum over (slice, domain) of ceil(members / N) / SM count; printed to <run>/predictions.txt before any cell runs). Cells (run_domain.sh; all SMs, lockstep start, 24 MB L2-resident footprint, ncu --cache-control none, first launch of a cell dropped, two runs). TMA: table cells m0 (disjoint control), single bits m1 m2 m4 m8 m16 m32 m64, groups m3 m7 m15 m31 m63 m255, halfx (inside every block, SM e of one pair with SM e of the next pair: different pairs, same block), gpcx (SM i of the first block of a placement domain with SM i of its second block), speca (first block with the block of the highest ids), blk (a block per slice), gpc (a placement domain per slice); by block index: group 2 and 4, consecutive and far, and a rotated group-2 control; start offset cells m1 and halfx with member 1 later by 128 / 256 / 512 cycles; mc2 (cluster of two, rank 0 multicasts every tile to both CTAs). cp.async (one warp): m0 m1 halfx gpcx speca blk gpc, and m1 / halfx with offsets 256 and 1024. Predictions for the cells that separate the candidates (pair | block | gpc): halfx h100 1.000 | 0.515 | 0.545, b300 1.000 | 0.581 | 0.595; gpcx h100 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.576, b300 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.581; m16 h100 1.000 | 0.758 | 0.758, b300 1.000 | 0.784 | 0.784; m32 1.000 | 0.727 | 0.727 and 1.000 | 0.784 | 0.784; m64 b300 1.000 | 0.892 | 0.892; blk (N = 4 on h100, 3 on b300) 0.500 | 0.258 | 0.273 and 0.500 | 0.392 | 0.399; cells grouped by block index are predicted with the same formula from the SM ids each CTA records. Validity: m0 and the rotated control within 0.9..1.1, m1 at most 0.6, every SM id present once in every table cell; otherwise nothing is concluded for that request kind on that device. Decision, per request kind and device, both runs agreeing: halfx 'shares' if its ratio is nearer to the block prediction than to 1, gpcx 'shares' if nearer to the gpc prediction than to 1; domain = pair if neither shares, block if only halfx shares, gpc if both share, undecided if only gpcx shares. Consistency required before any rule: m16, m32 (and m64 on b300) each nearer to the chosen domain's prediction than to the rejected ones wherever those differ by more than 0.05, and the consecutive / far group-2 cells within 0.1 of the chosen domain's prediction from their recorded SM ids; a failed check is reported as mixed and no rule follows. Requests per read inside the chosen domain: N* = argmin over N in 2..6 of the mean |ratio - prediction(N)| over blk, gpc, m31, m63, m255, reported with its error next to the installed value; the installed value is replaced only if both runs give the same N* and its mean error is lower than the installed value's by more than 0.03. Start offsets: shared fraction m(D) = clamp((1 - r(D)) / (1 - r(0)), 0, 1); the offset where m crosses 0.5 (linear interpolation) is reported for halfx next to m1 of the same run; a difference of more than 25 percent in both runs is reported as a second window and not installed in this step. Multicast: mc2 with r_tex in 0.45..0.55 means one L2 read is counted against one delivery per receiving SM, and simulated ratios of multicast kernels have to count deliveries the same way before they are compared with hardware; about 1.0 means a multicast is one delivery. cp.async offset cells also report the mean stream cycles of member 0 and member 1: a member-1 stream shorter by about its start offset would mean the follower catches up, and the slow decay with the offset in shared_read_unsaturated (b300 about 1700 cycles, h100 none within 2048) then reads as catch-up rather than as a window; reported only. Use: if a request kind's domain is block or gpc on a device, the engine keys its merge entries by (sector, domain id of the requesting SM) with the id per SM from the device's SM topology table instead of floor(SM id / domain_sms); SM ids whose membership these cells do not establish (speca, the pairs after the last blocks) keep their pair; evidence experimental. If TMA and cp.async disagree, the rule is per request kind. Window and requests per read otherwise stay as installed. No value is fitted to kernel cycles; the kernel counters above are a later check of the rule, not its source.

addenda.name: read_domain_result
addenda.written: after the data (fg-line-mem/domain/{h100,b300}; H100 GPU-e76c5c58, B300 GPU-adc54988; 42 cells x 2 runs each, no failed cell, two retained launches per cell; readers read_domain.py and fg-line-mem/tools/domain_fit.py)
addenda.text: Ratios below are srcunit_tex reads per delivered sector (r_all equals them within 0.01 on these L2-resident cells), mean of the four retained launches, h100 | b300. Validity holds for both request kinds on both devices: m0 1.000 | 1.000, rotated control 0.99 | 1.00, m1 0.50-0.52. Multicast: mc2 0.500 | 0.500, so one multicast read is counted against one delivery per receiving SM. cp.async: halfx 0.528 | 0.632 (block prediction 0.515 | 0.581-0.595), gpcx 0.592 | 0.632 (gpc prediction 0.576 | 0.581): both share, declared outcome gpc on both devices. TMA on h100: halfx 0.607, gpcx 0.607, both nearer to the sharing prediction than to 1, declared outcome gpc; consistency holds (m16 0.773 against 0.758, m32 0.736 against 0.727, m2 0.970 against 0.970, consecutive pairs 0.51, far pairs 1.00). TMA on b300: halfx 0.888 and gpcx 0.839 are nearer to 1, so the declared outcome is pair, and the consistency check fails on m64 (0.929, nearer to the sharing prediction 0.892 than to 1; m16 0.960 and m32 0.918 are nearer to 1): by the declared rule b300 TMA is mixed and no rule follows. speca: h100 0.939 for both kinds, exactly the value if the eight pairs 124..131 share with the domain of SM 0, so those ids belong to that domain; b300 0.987 for cp.async (TMA alternates 0.987 / 1.000 between launches), i.e. one of the three pairs 142..147 shares with the first SMs of domain 0 and which one is not resolved, so 142..147 keep their pair. The placement domain of h100 with 124..131 added to domain 0, and of b300 as in the topology table, is called gpc below. Requests per read with that domain (mean error over blk, gpc, m31, m63, m255): h100 TMA N* = 4 in both runs (0.033; installed 4), h100 cp.async 4 (0.026), b300 TMA 3 (0.035; installed 3), b300 cp.async 4 (0.010 against 0.078 for 3). The b300 cp.async value meets the declared replacement condition but differs from the TMA value of the same leaf; the leaf stays 3 and the cp.async value is recorded (a per-kind count is not introduced in this step). Many-member cells against the two candidates: h100 gpc cell 0.277 TMA / 0.291 cp.async (gpc 0.273, pair 0.5), m255 0.271, blk 0.296 / 0.291; b300 gpc cell 0.321 / 0.283 (0.351, pair 0.5), m255 0.306, blk 0.344 / 0.312, m63 0.374 (0.399), m31 0.461 (0.480). Start offsets, shared fraction relative to offset 0: h100 TMA same pair 0.56 / 0.31 / 0.18 at 128 / 256 / 512 cycles (crossing 157), different pairs 0.52 / 0.34 / 0.24 (crossing 140): one window, and shorter than the installed 240 from the v1 sweep of another H100 (not changed here, three offsets only); b300 TMA same pair 0.56 / 0.08 / 0.00 (crossing 144, installed 145), different pairs 0.14 / 0.02 / 0.01 (crossing 74) from a base that shares only a quarter: a second, shorter window between pairs on b300, reported, not installed. cp.async: h100 no loss up to 1024 cycles for either relation; b300 same pair 1.00 / 0.84 at 256 / 1024, different pairs 0.78 / 0.50; the mean stream length of the delayed member differs from the leader's by -492..+194 cycles on h100 and by -1000..+6000 on b300, so a catch-up of the follower is not shown and the slow decay stays unexplained. Decision. h100 TMA, h100 cp.async, b300 cp.async: gpc by the declared rule. b300 TMA, changed after seeing the data and stated as such: the declared decision looked only at two-member cells, which on b300 TMA share between pairs of one gpc only partly (0.19-0.38 of the full saving, 0.65 for m64) and lose it within about 100 cycles of offset; every cell with four or more members per gpc is within 0.05 of the gpc prediction and 0.12-0.20 away from the pair prediction, and of the b300 TMA kernels with hardware counters (fg-fa3/hwmet) eight share more on hardware than the pair rule simulates (reads per delivered sector 0.69-0.89 against simulated 0.94-1.00; also FAF-BWD-BF16-1C-S05 0.49 against 0.81), one does not (CUF-DSL-BS-GRP-C04 0.88 against 0.86) and one shares nothing in either (MLF-MLSPF-H64-C08). The gpc domain is therefore applied to b300 TMA too; the two-member cells between pairs (predicted 0.58-0.60, measured 0.84-0.89) and m16 / m32 (0.784 against 0.96 / 0.92) are kept as counterexamples of that choice, with the shorter between-pair window as the open explanation. Installed: memory.l2_merge domain_gpc = 1 on both devices (evidence experimental, source l2_merge.<device>.read_domain) and the gpc column of the h100 SM topology table (placement domains 0..7, ids 124..131 in 0); window_cycles, max_requests_per_read and domain_sms (the fallback for SMs without a gpc) unchanged. Not established: which of 142..147 belongs to domain 0 on b300; whether 120..123 share inside placement domains 6 / 7 on h100 (taken from the dispatch order); the between-pair window on b300; why two cp.async members of one pair on h100 with four warps share only two thirds.

addenda.name: read_domain_kernel_check
addenda.written: after the full-GPU round r23 (fg-line-mem/full-r23, engine aa34eb7d with domain_gpc = 1 for every merging request kind) and the hardware counters of 38 kernels (fg-gemm/merge-hwmet, fg-fa3/hwmet, fg-line-mem/hwmet; table by fg-line-mem/tools/r_table.py)
addenda.text: The check announced in read_domain: simulated L2 reads per delivered sector against hardware (srcunit_tex reads / xbar2l1tex sectors of the measured launch; a multicast load counts one read and one delivery per receiving SM, as mc2 showed, so simulated deliveries are taken per receiving SM). Kernel cycles are not used. TMA kernels, hardware | pair rule (r22) | gpc rule (r23): h100 cublas_bf16_bigK_00 0.500 | 0.667 | 0.441, cublas_fp8_bigK_00 / _02 0.420 / 0.415 | 0.750 | 0.406, cublas_bf16_skinny_00 0.833 | 0.833 | 0.790, cutlass_sparse_00 0.715 | 0.772 | 0.634, deepgemm_einsum_00 / _03 / _06 / _08 0.725 / 0.673 / 0.566 / 0.654 | 0.956 / 0.956 / 0.801 / 0.968 | 0.756 / 0.727 / 0.643 / 0.551, deepgemm_einsum_04 0.838 | 0.667 | 0.667, deepgemm_bf16_mgroup_contiguous_01 0.630 | 0.905 | 0.708, fa3_fwd_hdim_small_05 0.736 | 0.921 | 0.597: mean absolute difference 0.21 with the pair rule, 0.07 with the gpc rule (twelve kernels; the gpc rule shares too much on einsum_08, hdim_small_05 and cutlass_sparse_00, both rules share too much on einsum_04). b300 BLF-FP8-C02 / BLF-BF16-C13 / BLF-MXFP8-C01 / BLF-EPI-RELUBIAS-C06 0.71-0.73 | 0.99-1.00 | 0.74-0.77, CUF-C74-STREAMK-C06 0.885 | 1.000 | 0.807, CUF-C76-CONV-WGRAD-S01 / S02 0.590 / 0.696 | 0.884 / 0.944 | 0.703 / 0.858, CUF-DSL-DENSE-PERSIST-C04 0.687 | 0.937 | 0.816, DGF-KG-FP8-TN-R01 / R05 0.885 / 0.836 | 0.996 / 0.990 | 0.864 / 0.743, FAF-BWD-BF16-1C-S05 0.488 | 0.806 | 0.533: the gpc rule is nearer in all eleven (mean absolute difference 0.24 with the pair rule, 0.07 with the gpc rule). Not comparable and left out: kernels whose simulated request count is under half of the delivered sectors (CUF-DSL-BS-GRP-C04, CUF-DSL-BS-NVF4-V16-R05, FIF-BS-SM103-NVF4-C05, MLF-MLSPF-H64-C08) and kernels without shared reads. So the after-data choice of the gpc domain for b300 TMA is not contradicted by kernels, and the h100 TMA choice is supported. cp.async kernels (h100 only): triton_matmul_bf16_03 / fp16_12 / fp8_23 0.862 / 0.873 / 0.905 | 0.934 / 0.953 / 1.019 | 0.801 / 0.769 / 0.807, cutlass_dense_cpasync_05 / _06 0.911 / 0.880 | 0.856 / 0.825 | 0.672 / 0.648: the gpc rule shares 0.06-0.24 more than hardware in all five (mean absolute difference 0.15 against 0.08 for the pair rule). The one-warp cp.async cells do share inside a gpc on h100, but the four-warp cells of shared_read_domain already shared less (all SMs on one region 0.50 against 0.31 with one warp, one pair 0.63 against 0.50; b300 0.42 against 0.28 and 0.51) and these kernels issue cp.async from every warp. Changed after this check: domain_gpc becomes an enum by request kind - 1 = TMA / bulk tensor loads, 2 = those and cp.async; h100 installs 1 (cp.async stays on the pair domain), b300 installs 2 (cp.async gpc by the declared rule of read_domain_result; no b300 cp.async kernel with shared reads has counters, so that part is unchecked). Open: why cp.async sharing between pairs falls with the number of issuing warps on h100 (a per-warp or per-request limit of the path is a guess, not measured); the between-pair window on b300; requests of different kinds do not share a merge entry in the engine (not measured either way).

addenda.text: Reads per delivered sector, hardware | pair rule (r22) | installed rule (r24). h100, eleven TMA kernels: mean absolute difference 0.20 with the pair rule, 0.07 with the installed rule, nearer in eight (cublas_int8_big_square_02 0.542 | 0.751 | 0.562, deepgemm_bf16_dense_02 0.384 | 0.809 | 0.403, deepgemm_bf16_mgroup_contiguous_02 0.464 | 0.906 | 0.518, cutlass_f16bf16_dense_tma_pingpong_07 0.602 | 0.970 | 0.689, triton_p9_matmul_descriptor_persistent_ws_00 0.719 | 0.988 | 0.671, triton_grouped_gemm_tma_02 0.754 | 0.966 | 0.644, cutlass_sparse_08 0.688 | 0.820 | 0.730, cublas_int8_bigK_00 0.643 | 0.750 | 0.599); the installed rule shares too much in three where the pair rule was already near (cublas_int8_bigK_02 0.593 | 0.600 | 0.503, cublas_tf32_bigK_01 0.653 | 0.667 | 0.528, cutlass_sparse_02 0.754 | 0.780 | 0.663). b300, twelve kernels: 0.23 against 0.06, nearer in all twelve (FAF-FWD-GQA-NOPACK-S04 0.324 | 0.766 | 0.434, FAF-FWD-SINK-1C-C06 0.390 | 0.759 | 0.466, CUF-DSL-DENSE-PERSIST-2CTA-P01 0.832 | 1.000 | 0.760, FIF-TGV-T18-C05 0.898 | 1.000 | 0.899, TRF-TUT-ATTN-FWD-FP16-CAUSAL-C05 0.674 | 0.860 | 0.809). These are the kernels that became faster than hardware in cycles (b300 twelve of twelve); their amount of sharing is now within 0.07 of hardware on average, so what makes them too fast is not how many reads are shared. Not attributed. One candidate was checked against existing data and is not supported as stated: the engine lets a request that rides on another SM's read skip its own SM's L2 port; the TMA cells of read_domain stream 31.1 (h100) / 28.2 (b300) bytes per cycle per SM whether shared or not, but that probe is bound by its per-SM stream rate either way (v1 addendum), and the v2 LDG cells differ by device - h100 delivers more per SM when reads are shared (58 / 103 bytes per cycle at G = 2 / 4 against 30 disjoint and 50 / 67 rotated), b300 the same 100-104 in lockstep and rotated form. Whether a rider occupies its SM's port needs its own cells.

addenda.name: merge_mechanics
addenda.written: before any data of these cells; the numbers quoted as known are from ldgsts-share / ldgsts-share4 and read_domain
addenda.text: Open after read_domain: (1) with four warps per CTA two cp.async SMs of one pair share only two thirds on h100 (0.63, one warp 0.50; b300 0.51 either way) and a whole card on one region 0.50 / 0.42 instead of 0.31 / 0.28; (2) cp.async sharing does not fall with the start offset as TMA sharing does; (3) how many requests one read serves; (4) on b300 two TMA SMs of different pairs share only partly. Known and relevant: in the four-warp h100 cells the L2-side read rate is 6.0-6.9 TB/s whether shared or not, next to 7.4 TB/s unshared (the installed GPU-wide L2 read rate 7.6), and the shared cells deliver 10.3-12.0 TB/s with a group latency of 570-720 cycles against 1030 unshared; with one warp the aggregate is 4.7 TB/s and latency 420. So on h100 the two-thirds cells are the ones where the unshared stream is already at the L2 read limit. Probe changes: a table member 65535 keeps that SM's CTA idle (both probes); ldgsts_loaded --pace P issues round r at start + r x P cycles and waits it before the next (one group in flight, so a start offset cannot be caught up), counts rounds that started more than 32 cycles late, and records 64 globaltimer stamps of thread 0 per CTA. Tables: domain_tables.py <device> <topology> <dir> mechanics (gpc = the topology table's column). Cells (run_mechanics.sh, ncu --cache-control none, first launch dropped, two runs; r = srcunit_tex reads per delivered sector). A, where the limit sits (cp.async, 1 / 4 / 8 warps): unshared streams all_m0 (every SM), g1_m0 (the 16-18 SMs of one gpc, the rest idle), t1_m0 (one pair in each gpc, 16 SMs), g2_m0 (two whole gpcs), t2_m0 (two pairs in each gpc); pair-shared streams all_m1, g1_m1, t1_m1; k2x (two SMs of different pairs per gpc). Readings fixed here. Throughput: with c(x) the per-CTA bytes per cycle at four warps, the L2 read limit is per gpc if c(g1_m0) <= 1.15 c(all_m0) and c(t1_m0) >= 1.3 c(all_m0); it is card-wide if c(g1_m0) and c(t1_m0) are within 15 percent of each other and both >= 1.3 c(all_m0); anything else is reported as mixed. Sharing: (S) lost under the card-wide limit if r(t1_m1) and r(g1_m1) <= 0.55 where r(all_m1) >= 0.6; (G) lost under a per-gpc limit if r(g1_m1) >= 0.6 and r(t1_m1) <= 0.55; (W) a property of the warp count if all three are >= 0.6; b300, whose pair cells stay at 0.51, is read on the eight-warp cells the same way and on k16 at four warps (0.42 before) against k16 at one warp. B, requests per read (one warp cp.async, and TMA): k2 k3 k4 k6 k8 k12 k16 = the first k SMs of every gpc on one slice, the rest idle, and g1_all; predicted ceil(k / N) / k with the installed N (h100 4: 0.5, 0.333, 0.25, 0.333, 0.25, 0.25, 0.25; b300 3: 0.5, 0.333, 0.5, 0.333, 0.375, 0.333, 0.375); N* = argmin over N in 2..8 of the mean absolute difference over k >= 3, per request kind, device and run; the installed value changes only if both runs give the same N*, its error is lower than the installed value's by more than 0.03, and the two request kinds agree on the device (otherwise both are recorded and a per-kind count is left for a later step). C, which pairs (one warp cp.async, and TMA): x1 x2 x3 x4 = SM e of pair i with SM e of pair i + d of the same gpc, the rest idle; full sharing is 0.5. Shared fraction f(d) = 2 (1 - r); uniform if the four f are within 0.15 of each other, pair-specific if some are >= 0.8 and others <= 0.3; reported, no rule from it in this step. D, the cp.async window without catch-up (one warp, every SM active, pace 600 cycles): m1 (the two SMs of a pair) and xp (SM e of a pair with SM e of the next pair of its gpc) with the second member later by 0, 64, 128, 192, 256, 384, 512, 1024 cycles, and xpr (members swapped) at 128 and 256. A cell is valid if fewer than 1 percent of its rounds were late and the recorded start difference of the members (median over the stamps) is within 40 ns of the offset. Shared fraction m(D) = (1 - r(D)) / (1 - r(0)). Readings: in flight only if m <= 0.2 at 512 and 1024; retained if m >= 0.8 at 1024; otherwise the crossing of 0.5 is reported. If in flight and the crossing is within 25 percent of the TMA crossing measured on the device (h100 157 same pair / 140 between pairs, b300 144 / 74), cp.async follows the installed window and the missing decay of the unpaced cells is closed-loop catch-up; if retained, cp.async needs its own, longer window and its length is not known from these cells (1024 is a lower bound). Use: A decides whether the reduced sharing of many-warp cp.async is a consequence of an L2 read limit the engine already has (then the engine's merge has to be tested under that limit by replay before any rule) or needs a new fact; a per-gpc read limit would be a change of memory.shared_service and is only reported here. Nothing is fitted to kernel cycles.

addenda.name: merge_mechanics_result
addenda.written: after the data (fg-line-mem/mechanics/{h100,b300}; H100 GPU-8b1c0a21, B300 GPU-adc54988; 73 cells x 2 runs each, no failed cell; readers read_mechanics.py, fg-line-mem/tools/mech_fit.py)
addenda.text: Probe defect, found in the data: the loop of the cp.async probe became slower with the stamp code (measured: about 280 more cycles per round on h100 and 140 on b300; read off the SASS, not timed separately: a division by a run-time value on a branch only thread 0 takes); one warp now delivers 5.2 (h100) / 8.4 (b300) bytes per cycle per CTA where the unchanged probe delivered 18 / 19, and a paced round takes longer than the 600-cycle pace. Consequences: part A reaches the h100 read limit only with eight warps (the readings were declared at four), and every part-D cell fails its validity rule (h100: all rounds late; b300: 40-83 percent late). Parts B and C use one warp or TMA and are not affected. B, requests per read: h100 N* = 4 for both request kinds in both runs (mean error 0.02-0.04; TMA k = 2 / 3 / 4 / 6 / 8 / 12 / 16 gives 0.500 / 0.333 / 0.26 / 0.334 / 0.30 / 0.28 / 0.27 against ceil(k / 4) / k = 0.5 / 0.333 / 0.25 / 0.333 / 0.25 / 0.25 / 0.25); b300 N* = 3 for both kinds in both runs (0.07-0.08; 0.11-0.15 for 4). Both equal the installed values; the b300 cp.async value 4 read off the blk / gpc cells in read_domain_result is withdrawn. On b300 the third SM (the first of the next pair) does not join: k3 0.62-0.64 TMA, 0.52-0.55 cp.async against 0.333. C, pairs of one gpc, shared fraction f = 2 (1 - r) at pair distance 1 / 2 / 3 / 4: h100 TMA 0.82-0.83 / 0.82 / 0.87-0.95 / 0.78-0.81 and cp.async 0.73-0.78 / 0.73-0.77 / 0.88-0.94 / 0.77-0.79, uniform by the declared rule except cp.async run b (spread 0.17); b300 TMA 0.35 / 0.47-0.50 / 0.38-0.40 / 0.43-0.48 (uniform, partial), b300 cp.async 0.33-0.36 / 0.51-0.58 / 0.19-0.25 / 0.63-0.68 (neither uniform nor pair-specific by the thresholds; even distances share more). Two SMs of different pairs with the rest of the card idle (k2x, TMA): h100 0.500, i.e. complete where the same relation shares 0.8 with every SM active; b300 0.928, i.e. almost none where it shares 0.35-0.5 with every SM active. A, throughput at eight warps, bytes per cycle per CTA unshared: h100 one pair in each gpc 39.8 (16 SMs, bound by the probe), one whole gpc 31.4 (16 SMs, 953 B/ns), two whole gpcs 31.5, every SM 28.8 (6.5 TB/s); c(g1) <= 1.15 c(all) and c(t1) >= 1.3 c(all) hold, so the h100 L2 read limit is per gpc, about 0.95 TB/s each, and eight of them are the installed GPU-wide 7.6 TB/s. At four warps nothing is limited (20.6 in every cell), so by the letter of the declared four-warp reading the result is 'mixed'; the eight-warp reading is taken because the slower probe moved the operating point, stated here as a change after data. b300 reaches no limit in any cell (61.7 everywhere, 18.3 TB/s with every SM against 20.1 installed): undecided. A, sharing of one pair (0.5 = complete), h100 one / four / eight warps: one pair per gpc 0.50-0.56 / 0.75-0.87 / 0.95, one whole gpc 0.50-0.62 / 0.79-0.84 / 0.68-0.70, every SM 0.54-0.57 / 0.75-0.79 / 0.54-0.55; b300 0.50-0.56 / 0.93-0.95 / 0.97, 0.50-0.67 / 0.89-0.96 / 0.97, 0.55-0.64 / 0.93-0.94 / 0.97. By the declared readings this is (W), a loss that comes with the warp count and not with a limit - but the eight-warp h100 cells add what none of the declared readings covered: where the gpc or the card is at its read limit the sharing comes back (0.69, 0.55) and where it is not it is almost gone (0.95). The recorded start times go with it: the two SMs of a pair are at least one timer tick (256 ns, about 500 cycles) apart in 4-20 percent of the stamps of the one-warp cells and in 56-94 percent of the stamps of the cells that share little (b300 four warps 70-78 percent at r 0.94; h100 eight warps 75 percent at 0.95, 59 percent at 0.69, 44 percent at 0.55). The unchanged probe kept its pairs together at four warps on b300 (0.51 in shared_read_domain) and this one does not, with nothing but the loop body changed. So how much a multi-warp pair shares is not a property of the warp count: it changed with the loop body alone, it goes with the two streams being apart in time, and on h100 it comes back where the gpc or the card is at its read limit. Which way the dependence runs is not established (streams that share get their data together and so stay together). That a read can be joined for as long as it waits, queueing included, would fit all three and is not tested here. D (invalid cells, reported): h100 same pair with 1024 cycles offset, one group in flight: the recorded start difference falls from 768 ns to 0 within the first ten stamps (about 600 rounds) and stays 0, r 0.50 at every offset - the follower catches up, seen directly (the pace did not hold it because every round was late; what makes the follower faster before it has caught up is not known); between pairs most slices stay at 0 and a few drift apart by 8-40 microseconds while r stays 0.515. b300 same pair: the offset is kept (512 ns recorded at 1024 cycles) and r goes 0.52 / 0.62-0.65 / 0.60-0.66 / 0.65-0.68 / 0.71-0.77 at 0 / 64 / 128-384 / 512 / 1024 cycles, a shared fraction of about 0.75 from 64 cycles on and 0.5 at 1024; between pairs 0.72 at 0 and 0.85 at 1024 (0.595 = complete). Not concluded from D: any window. Open after this: the part-D question with a probe whose loop is not slowed and a pace above the round time; whether the b300 read limit is per gpc; whether an in-flight read can be joined for as long as it waits.

addenda.name: merge_mechanics_rerun

addenda.name: async_copy_window
addenda.text: Question: the cp.async sharing window below 64 cycles. Cells (run_window.sh; one warp, every SM active, pace 1200, cp.async, two runs): m1 (the two SMs of a pair) and xp (SM e of a pair with SM e of the next pair of its gpc) with the second member later by 0, 8, 16, 24, 32, 40, 48, 64, 96 cycles. Validity: late rounds under 1 percent; r(0) of m1 at most 0.62. Derivation, the v1 rule of this protocol: shared fraction m(D) = clamp((1 - r(D)) / (1 - r(0)), 0, 1), window = the offset where m crosses 0.5 by linear interpolation between the bracketing cells, per run, from m1; the xp crossing is reported next to it. Install: new field memory.l2_merge async_copy_window_cycles = the mean of the two runs if they agree within 15 percent (evidence experimental, source l2_merge.<device>.async_copy_window); the engine uses it instead of window_cycles for async copies (cp.async); a device whose runs disagree, or whose m does not cross between two measured offsets, gets no field and keeps window_cycles. With it h100 cp.async moves to the gpc domain (domain_gpc = 2) only if the kernel check passes: the five h100 cp.async kernels with counters (triton_matmul_bf16_03 / fp16_12 / fp8_23, cutlass_dense_cpasync_05 / 06) must have a smaller mean absolute difference of reads per delivered sector to hardware than the installed pair rule gives (0.075); otherwise the field is installed and h100 cp.async stays on the pair domain. Kernel cycles decide nothing.

addenda.name: async_copy_window_service
addenda.written: before the engine has the rule and before any arm of it
addenda.text: Candidate, from the cells above, no new number: a read opened by an async copy can be joined from its issue until async_copy_window_cycles after the read has been served by the shared L2 (or DRAM) read service, i.e. expiry = max(issue, time the leader's sector leaves the shared read service) + async_copy_window_cycles instead of issue + window. Without queueing this is the measured window; at a read limit the interval grows by the time the leader waits. Field memory.l2_merge async_copy_window_from_service (boolean). Check, same five h100 kernels and the same counters, two arms (pair domain; gpc domain = domain_gpc 2): mean absolute difference of reads per delivered sector to hardware. Outcomes fixed here: (1) the pair arm is below 0.075 -> install async_copy_window_cycles with async_copy_window_from_service = 1 on both devices (b300 has no cp.async kernel with counters and shared reads; it follows on the direction of its eight-warp cells, stated as unchecked), and h100 cp.async takes the gpc domain only if the gpc arm is below the pair arm; (2) the pair arm is not below 0.075 -> neither field is installed on either device (the leaves are removed, cp.async keeps window_cycles and r24 stays the model), the measured windows stay recorded in this protocol as measured and not installed, and the rule for waiting reads is left open. Kernel cycles decide nothing. Not covered by this check: an engine replay of the mechanics cells themselves (needs traced captures of the probe).

addenda.text: Reads per delivered sector, hardware | r24 (window 240, pair) | window from service, pair | window from service, gpc: triton_matmul_bf16_03 0.862 | 0.934 | 0.853 | 0.507; triton_matmul_fp16_12 0.873 | 0.953 | 0.708 | 0.476; triton_matmul_fp8_23 0.905 | 1.019 | 1.019 | 0.868; cutlass_dense_cpasync_05 0.911 | 0.856 | 0.829 | 0.737; cutlass_dense_cpasync_06 0.880 | 0.825 | 0.820 | 0.714. Open: what a waiting read's joinable interval is (issue + 22 cycles shares too little on kernels at the read limit, until 22 cycles after the shared service too much on one of five); the engine code for both fields stays, off (fields absent), for the next attempt. addenda.name: b300_async_kernel_check
addenda.written: before the counters and before the arms; seen: the full-GPU rounds m1 / m2 (fg-line-mem/full-m1, full-m2) in which eight b300 cp.async kernels became 10-25 percent faster once the converter stopped giving every commit_group group the 32-copy completion (TRF-TUT-MATMUL-FP16-C02 / C04 / C06 0.85-0.92 -> 0.69-0.70 of hardware, TRF-TUT-MATMUL-FP8-C04 / C06, TRF-TUT-GROUP-GEMM-PTR-C03 / R02, TRF-TUT-PERSIST-NAIVE-C04 0.93-1.06 -> 0.81-0.83), and their simulated reads per request 0.45-0.63
addenda.text: The b300 cp.async part of the installed rule (gpc domain, window_cycles 145) was installed without any kernel with counters (read_domain_kernel_check). These eight kernels are that check; they are picked by how far they moved, their counters do not exist yet. Hardware: reads per delivered sector as in read_domain_kernel_check (fg-line-mem/hwmet3/bw). Arms (fg-line-mem/bw-async-arm, engine and clone of round m2): the installed rule; pair = cp.async in the pair domain with window_cycles; gpcw / pairw = gpc / pair domain with async_copy_window_cycles 12.5 (the measured b300 cp.async window); gpcws / pairws = the same with the window counted from the end of the shared read service. Prediction: hardware 0.80-0.95 as on the h100 triton kernels (0.86-0.91), so the installed rule shares far too much. Decision fixed here: mean absolute difference of reads per delivered sector over the kernels that have counters and whose simulated request count is within 3 percent of the delivered sectors (otherwise deliveries are taken from hardware, as r_table.py does); the arm with the smallest difference is installed for b300 cp.async if it is below the installed rule's by more than 0.03; if two arms are within 0.02 of each other the one with fewer unmeasured parts is taken, in this order: gpcw (domain and window both measured on b300), pairw, gpcws, pairws, pair. If no arm beats the installed rule by 0.03 nothing changes. Kernel cycles decide nothing. The h100 kernels that moved with the converter change (fg-line-mem/hwmet3/hp: triton_grouped_gemm_02 / 03, flashinfer_batch_decode_paged_00, flashinfer_single_decode_00, flashinfer_single_prefill_02, triton_attn_bwd_01) get counters for the record; no h100 rule depends on them here.
